shots.note: The architecture is good: a stepped terracotta tower roof with dark-oak ribs, a windowed cupola with a finial, timber framing over white plaster, big glazing, a porch, a dormered wing, a pond, cherry and autumn trees, lantern posts and a framed flower garden. Problems: (1) It is not golden hour. The sky is midday blue with only a faint warm band at the far left, the facade is lit flat, and the sun shows as a hard white square cut off at the top-left edge. Fix: set the time to about 12300-12600, aim the camera so the sunset gradient sits behind the building, and keep the sun disc out of frame or fully in it. (2) Cohesion: the blue-black deepslate roof on the right wing is a second roof language that clashes with the terracotta tower and is not in the palette. Fix: re-roof the wing in terracotta/granite or dark oak with copper ridge trim. The terraced dirt-sided hills on the right look unfinished. Fix: grass-slab or moss-carpet the step edges. (3) Composition: the foreground garden is cut off at the bottom-left, and the right third is empty grass and a dirt strip. Fix: shift the camera left about 10% or add a tree or bench cluster at the right to frame the building. (4) Character/aliveness: no agents or motion are visible, so the place reads as empty. Fix: put one agent on the porch or path and add a chimney campfire-smoke plume or a cat or bee. (5) Legibility/clarity: the doc's far-distance layer (beacon or lamp colors showing status) is missing. The screens through the windows are unreadable smudges. Fix: put status lamps in the cupola or under the eaves, one per agent in its state color, plus a sign at the entrance.

Strongest world shot. The tall ceiling with beams, the copper chandelier on chains, the terracotta floor border and the hologram plinth make a real focal point, and the goal HUD reads instantly: progress ring, '2 of 9 done', and '2 need you' in clay. Problems: (1) Cohesion: three panel styles in one frame (dark ink goal HUD, dark Marlow nameplate, white decision bubble). The doc calls for matte paper panels. Fix: render the goal HUD as a paper panel with ink text and a brass border, or make every world callout one consistent style. (2) Legibility: the most important text is truncated. The goal ends 'filter with `no...', the nameplate says 'asking you about `not...' and the question is cut. Fix: wrap the goal to 3 lines and let the decision bubble wrap to 3 lines before using an ellipsis. Also, '39%' next to '2 of 9 tasks done' reads as a contradiction, because it is weighted partial credit. Fix: label it ('39% weighted') or drive the ring from the done count. (3) Composition: the task wall at the left is a skewed, cropped sliver with text fragments ('ses:', 'failing') bleeding in at the edge. Fix: pull the camera in or rotate it so the wall is either fully readable or out of frame. The nameplate and decision bubble both point at Marlow, which is redundant clutter. Fix: hide the nameplate's activity line while a decision bubble is shown for that agent. (4) Lighting: pleasant but flat ambient. The hologram cone is faint, and the upper beams and coffers go dark. Fix: add hidden light strips behind the beam trim and give the projector cone a stronger emissive. (5) Aliveness: Marlow's '!' is hidden behind the HUD and he stands stiff. Fix: keep the '!' above the HUD z-order and add an idle sway or a head turn toward the camera.

The kanban is crisp and quick to read: TODO, DOING, REVIEW and DONE columns with counts, paper cards with assignee avatars in agent colors, dependency text ('after t3, t4'), a red left border on the blocked card, 'CI failing' in red and greyed DONE cards. 9 cards, close to the target of 10. Problems: (1) Composition: the board fills only the middle ~45% of the frame and the bottom 55% of every column is empty bark. The rest of the frame is heavy dark oak recess and ceiling. Fix: move the camera closer so the board fills ~75% of the width, and size columns to their content or add a footer strip (goal/progress) to use the space. (2) Lighting: it is the darkest interior shot, with a dim alcove and a black ceiling mass, which breaks the 'no dark corners' rule. Fix: add a hidden light bar under the top trim washing down the board, plus side sconces. (3) Cohesion: the dark-oak-log bark texture behind the cards is noisy and very dark. Fix: back the board with a stripped-oak or cork/paper panel and keep the dark oak only as the frame. (4) Clarity: the REVIEW card for t4 shows a grey (idle) dot, even though t4 is awaiting the user's merge. The wall never shows that the user is the blocker. Fix: give review-awaiting-user cards the pulsing clay dot and a 'your merge' tag. Also, the blocked card's reason is cut off ('needs Blendi's npm...'). Fix: allow a 2-line subtext on blocked cards. (5) Character/aliveness: no agents and no motion. Fix: animate card moves between columns, add a subtle pulse on cards needing the user, and put an agent pinning a card or a plant and lamp nearby.

Good ideas: a streaming log with red and green diff highlighting and a cursor on a brass-framed emissive monitor, status gems in frames above each desk (gold for thinking, teal for working), a thinking sparkle over Tove, and seated agents. Problems: (1) Legibility: Juniper's floating nameplate sits on top of her own monitor and hides the code ('eturn i >= 0...'). Tove's nameplate covers Tove's monitor too, and Tove's monitor text is far too small to read. Fix: anchor nameplates above the head with a minimum screen-space offset, and fade or shrink them when they overlap a monitor the camera is focused on. (2) Composition: Marlow's huge cropped monitor ('cre..., write..., reque...') bleeds in at the right edge and pulls the eye, and the foreground desk block takes the bottom-center. Fix: reframe so Juniper and her monitor are the clear subject (camera lower and to her side), with Marlow's monitor fully out of frame. (3) Character: we only see the backs of both agents' heads, and Tove's head reads at an odd tilted angle. Juniper's dark hair texture is noisy. Fix: frame from a 3/4 front angle so the face and the colored scarf or badge show, and clean Juniper's hair to a 3-4 tone ramp. (4) Clarity: Tove's activity is truncated ('outlining the Tags do...'). Fix: wrap or shorten the activity text to fit, e.g. 'drafting Tags docs'. (5) Cohesion: the blank cream frame blocks beside each status gem look like empty paintings. Fix: use them for agent name plaques or task IDs.

The warm studio comes through: lanterns hanging from chains, beams, bookshelves, a cream frieze, carpets, plants, and Marlow's activity log readable on the back wall. Wren on the sofa is a charming, distinct character. Problems: (1) Clarity: Rowan's and Tove's nameplates float with no visible bodies (hidden behind shelves or desks), so they read as orphan labels. Only Wren and a tiny Juniper are actually visible, short of the '3+ agents working' target. Fix: hide nameplates for occluded agents (or show a 'behind' leader line), and choose a camera that sees each station's occupant. (2) Composition: the foreground lounge (sofas, table, carpet) fills the bottom half while the actual work stations sit in the back third. Wide-FOV distortion stretches the edge furniture and the giant top-center lantern. The left edge is clutter: a large wood block, a fire cut off at the bottom-left, and an unreadable white object. Fix: raise the camera, narrow the FOV to ~70, aim over the lounge toward the desks, and crop out the left-edge props. (3) Legibility: Tove's plate is truncated ('outlining the Tags do') and partly overlapped by Wren's plate and a stray clay '!'. Monitors at this distance are smudges. Fix: de-overlap nameplates in screen space, and show only name + state dot at far distance. (4) Character: apart from Wren, agents are tiny or invisible. A dark speck particle near Wren's head reads as a glitch. Fix: replace it with the doc's clay '!' or nothing.

Marlow (glasses, beard, navy suit, gold badge) has a strong silhouette, and the clay '!' and the podium embers signal waiting. Problems: (1) Cohesion: the alcove's thin glowing salmon outline looks like a debug bounding box or a selection highlight, not architecture. Fix: replace it with real trim (cut-copper or terracotta pilasters with hidden light behind) or a soft glow on the floor in front of the podium. (2) Clarity: this is meant to be an 'open decision', but only the teaser shows. The question is truncated in both the nameplate and the bubble, and no options are visible (Yes/No or choices, the J key unlabeled). Fix: when the user is within ~4 blocks, expand the bubble into the full question plus 2-3 labeled options ('J open · 1 Yes · 2 No'). Show the second waiting decision's title too. (3) Composition: the podium is small and off-center, and the bottom third is empty birch floor. Marlow stands ~4 blocks from the podium, so they read as unrelated. Fix: move Marlow next to the podium facing the user and drop the camera so the podium and bubble form the focal point. (4) Lighting: flat ambient with a dark alcove interior and a blank white upper-right wall. Fix: warm light from under the podium and a hidden strip behind the alcove top trim, plus articulation (a frame or a shelf) on the white wall. (5) Legibility: the right-side mini screen ('Tests fail on t5 (tests 17, pass...') is cramped and truncated. Fix: give it fewer, larger lines, or drop it from this shot.

The console content is very good: '6 on shift' with face icons and state dots, per-line agent faces and colored names, the needs-you lines in clay or red, the test failure called out, and the @mention autocomplete with ghost text and a placeholder. Problems: (1) Cohesion: the autocomplete popup is a dark grey box, close to the default Minecraft GUI the doc bans, sitting on a cream paper panel. The console border is thin grey, not brass. Fix: style the popup as paper with an ink-and-clay selected row and a brass border, and give the console a brass border to match the diff and library modals. (2) Composition: the console takes the left ~63% while the input bar spans the full width, and the right third is a noisy close-up of azalea blocks. Marlow's nameplate is half-clipped behind the panel top edge. Fix: dim and blur the world behind the console (as the modals do), match the panel and input widths or center the panel, and hide world nameplates while the console is open. (3) Character: the faces are tiny 8px icons. Fix: show larger portraits in the header and in the autocomplete row. (4) Lighting: no treatment; the world shows at raw daylight. Fix: apply the same warm dim/vignette as the modals.

Near ship quality. Paper panel, brass border, clay rule, branch chips, tests-pass dot, +26/-5 that sums correctly across the files, file list with M badges, Wren's summary and Rowan's review notes, hunk header with an unchanged-line count, syntax highlighting, sage add-tint, and a clear button hierarchy (filled clay Merge, red-text Reject) with keybind hints. Problems: (1) Character: Wren's avatar is the only face, and it is small and static. Fix: a larger portrait with a pulsing clay 'waiting' ring. (2) Aliveness: the still shows nothing live. Fix: animate the 'Waiting for you' dot pulse, show a live 'tests: running/pass' chip, and add a relative-time ticker. Minor: the header's 'd3' is cryptic (label it 'decision 3' or drop it); code is set in the proportional pixel font, so alignment is fragile (a monospace pixel font would read better); the faux-bold headers look smudged; the left column has a big empty area under the notes.

A clean, well-organized memory screen: tabs with counts (All, Shared, Kit), a note list with author, scope and age, and a structured plan with Goal, Approach and Tasks, plus status dots and 'blocked: needs Blendi' in bold. Problems: (1) Clarity: t4 shows a gold (thinking) dot here, a grey (idle) dot on the task wall and a clay 'awaiting your merge' nameplate. That is three states for one task. Fix: drive every surface from a single status mapping (the doc's colors), so t4 is clay waiting-on-user everywhere. The trailing dots after '(after t2)' and '(after t3, t4)' look like more status for the task itself. Fix: render dependencies as small chips ('t2 ✓') instead of loose dots. (2) Character: only 8px author icons. Fix: a larger author portrait in the detail header. (3) Aliveness: static. Fix: highlight notes updated in the last minute with a soft clay fade-in and a live 'updated Ns ago'. Minor: the inline code chips (brass text on pale tan) are low-contrast, so darken the chip text to ink; a half-row is clipped at the fold (t8), so fade the bottom edge instead; the left list has ~40% empty space.

The same strong silhouette as the hero shot, with a starry sky, lit windows showing the chandelier, the goal hologram and monitors, and lantern posts on the path. Problems: (1) Lighting: the windows show the interior at normal brightness but don't glow, light doesn't spill onto the ground, and the facade, roof and cupola fall to murky dark. That reads as 'Minecraft house at night', not the cozy lit-from-within postcard. Fix: hidden light blocks behind window sills and under eaves to wash the facade, glowing lanterns at the porch and doors, light blocks under the flower beds so warm pools show on the ground, and a lit cupola as a beacon. (2) Clarity/legibility: from outside there is still no status signal, and the monitors are unreadable specks. Fix: the same per-agent status lamps in the cupola or eaves, which should look great at night. (3) Character/aliveness: no visible occupants or motion. Fix: put one agent silhouette visible in a lit window, and add fireflies or particles over the pond and garden. (4) Cohesion and composition carry over from qa01: the deepslate wing roof clashes, and the right third is empty.

overall: Not shippable against the doc's 'all ≥ 8' bar. The full-screen UI screens are close: diff review (qa08) and memory library (qa09) are polished and on-palette, and the console (qa07) and task wall (qa03) are legible and informative. The 3D world shots fall short on four recurring points. (1) The most important text is truncated: the goal, Marlow's question, the blocked card's reason and Tove's activity. (2) Nameplates collide with monitors and each other, or float with no visible body. (3) Lighting is flat or dark rather than warm golden-hour or hidden-light. The exterior lacks golden hour and any far-distance status layer, and the night shot doesn't glow. (4) Agents are rarely framed so their faces and appeal show. Across shots, task t4's status is shown in three different colors (grey on the wall, gold in the library, clay on the nameplate), which undermines the 5-second clarity the UI otherwise earns. Panel styles are mixed (dark goal HUD, dark autocomplete, white bubbles) where the doc asks for one matte-paper language. Average is roughly 6.6 overall: UI screens about 7.5, world shots about 6.
fixes: Single status source of truth: map every task and agent state to the doc's status colors once and use it on the task wall, library, nameplates and console. Make t4 'awaiting your merge' clay (waiting-on-user, pulsing) everywhere, not grey or gold.
Truncation pass: wrap the goal HUD to 3 lines, decision bubbles to 3 lines, blocked-card subtext to 2 lines and nameplate activity to a short verb phrase before ever using an ellipsis.

Nameplate layout: enforce a minimum offset above the head, de-overlap in screen space, hide plates for occluded agents, fade plates over a focused monitor, and suppress world plates while a console or modal is open.
Exterior far-distance status layer: per-agent status lamps in the cupola or under the eaves in state colors, visible in both qa01 and qa10.

qa01 time and camera: set the time to about 12300-12600 for real golden hour, keep the sun disc out of frame or fully in it, and frame tighter so the garden isn't cut and the empty right third shrinks.
Re-roof the right wing to match the terracotta/dark-oak/copper language (deepslate is off-palette), and grass or moss over the exposed dirt terrace edges.
Night lighting: hidden light behind window sills, under eaves and in flower beds for warm spill on the facade and ground, plus porch and door lanterns and a lit cupola.

Unify panel styling: goal HUD and autocomplete popup to matte paper with ink text and a thin brass border (no dark grey boxes), and give the console a brass border like the modals. Dim and blur the world behind the console.

Decision podium: replace the debug-looking glowing outline with real trim plus hidden light, move Marlow beside the podium facing the user, and expand to the full question plus labeled options when the user is near.
Task wall: frame closer (board ~75% of width), back the cards with a lighter panel instead of dark bark, add a down-wash light bar, and add a clay 'your merge' tag on review cards awaiting the user.

qa04 and qa05 cameras: show agents from a 3/4 front angle so faces and colored scarves read, narrow the FOV to ~70, aim over the lounge at the working stations, and crop out edge clutter (Marlow's cropped monitor, the left-edge props and fire).
Goal ring: label the weighted percentage or drive the ring from the done count so '39%' doesn't contradict '2 of 9 done'.

Aliveness in UI: pulsing clay waiting dots, live test-run chip in the diff header, larger agent portraits with state rings in the modal headers, and a fade-in highlight on recently updated memory notes.

shots.note: Strengths: a decent half-timbered build with big windows, a cupola, a flower garden, lantern posts and a pond, so it reads as architecture and not a box. Problems: it is not golden hour. The sky is mostly blue, a blown-out white sun square is cropped in the top-left corner, and the facade has flat light with no warm raking light. The building reads as a Tudor cottage rather than a 'Scandinavian studio / observatory'. Two roof materials fight each other: a clay-tile tower against a dark deepslate wing that is off-palette. The tower roof is a lumpy stepped helmet that overhangs its base, and the porch gable meets the tower awkwardly. Raw stepped terrain with exposed dirt sits at the right edge. A large empty lawn fills the middle ground. There is no sign of life: no agents, smoke, animals or motion. There is also no far-distance status signal (beacon or lamp), so the state of work cannot be read from outside. FIXES: (lighting) set the time to around 12300 with the sun low behind camera-left so warm light rakes the plaster, and keep the sun disc out of frame. (cohesion) use one roof language on both volumes, e.g. clay tile with dark-oak ridges and copper flashing, and reshape the tower roof into a clean bell/ogee or hip that doesn't overhang its base. (composition) bring the camera lower and closer so the building fills about 60% of the frame and the garden path works as a leading line. Landscape the dirt terraces on the right with stone retaining walls or planted terraces. (character/aliveness) have an agent walking the path, add chimney smoke, bees/birds, swaying banners. (clarity/legibility) put a status beacon in the cupola (clay pulsing because 2 need you), plus a small exterior sign/plaque with the goal name.

Strengths: a symmetrical room with a clear focal point (the clay plinth with the cyan core) and good materials: birch floor with a terracotta/walnut border, cream walls, copper, hanging lanterns. The goal summary ('2 of 9 done, 2 in progress, 1 in review, 2 need you') gives a lot of the state at a glance. Problems: the goal panel is a dark charcoal HUD slab, which breaks the 'matte paper panel with ink text' rule and clashes with the cream decision bubble beside it. It floats mid-air over the doorway, hides the room's depth and reads as a screen overlay rather than an in-world object. The goal text is truncated ('filter with `no...') on the hero UI. 39% doesn't match 2/9 done (22%), so users will question it. The task wall on the left is seen at an extreme angle and cut off by the frame edge, so it can't be read. The light is flat vanilla, and the upper wall bays are dull cream without hidden glow. Marlow stands stiffly in the mid-ground and his '!' is hard to see. The shot also seems to look out through a doorway rather than in from the entrance. FIXES: (cohesion/legibility) restyle the goal panel as cream paper with ink text and a brass border, and wrap the goal to 2-3 lines with no ellipsis. Either label the percentage as weighted or show task-based progress. (composition) lower and shrink the panel so it reads as a banner or hologram attached to the plinth and the doorway stays visible. Turn the camera or move the task wall so it isn't sliced at the left edge. (lighting) hide light blocks behind the dark-oak cornices and under the upper beams so the plaster bays glow warmly. (character/aliveness) Marlow should turn his head toward the user with a visible pulsing clay '!' and an idle gesture. Add drifting motes in the beam above the plinth.

Strengths: the cream cards with ink text, per-column header colors, agent face icons, dependency text ('after t3, t4'), the red 'CI failing' tag and the dimmed DONE cards are good information design, and the text is crisp. Problems: the board fills only about 45% of the frame width, and the cards fill only the top 45% of the board, so more than half the board is empty dark wood. Everything around it is dark walnut (frame, beam, ceiling, log backing), which makes the shot heavy and gloomy instead of 'pale birch & cream'. The board gets no light. There is no agent or motion anywhere. State is ambiguous: the TODO header shows a red dot next to '4', which reads as '4 blocked' when 1 is blocked. The REVIEW card (t4) has a grey idle dot even though it is awaiting the user's merge. Elsewhere t4 shows clay on the nameplate and brass in the library, so status colors are inconsistent across screens. FIXES: (composition) dolly in until the board fills about 80% of the frame, or make the board shorter and the cards larger so the columns fill it. (cohesion/lighting) replace the dark-oak log backing with birch or a cream cork texture, and hide lights behind the top trim to wash the board. (clarity) colour t4 clay and pulsing with an 'awaiting your merge' line. Replace the red-dot count with an explicit '1 blocked' chip. Use one status-color mapping across task wall, nameplates, library and console. (character/aliveness) have the planner agent stand at the board moving a card, add a subtle pulse on cards that need the user, and give the 'CI failing' tag a small shake or blink.

Strengths: Juniper is seated and typing at a brass-bezelled monitor that streams a real red/green diff. The status lamps above the desks (brass for thinking Tove, teal for working Juniper) work well for far-distance reading. Tove's yellow thinking sparkle is visible. Problems: Juniper's nameplate covers the left third of her monitor, hiding the code lines. Every code line is cut with '...', so the 'legible log' is half-legible. Marlow's monitor is sliced at the right edge and shows clipped words ('cre', 'write', 'reque'). A large dark chair block in the foreground hides Juniper's body. Both agents are seen from behind, so no faces show, and Juniper's head reads as a dark mass. The light is flat, with no glow from the monitor on the agent. FIXES: (legibility) offset nameplates up and away from screens, or fade them to about 40% when they overlap a monitor. Soft-wrap code at word boundaries instead of ellipsizing, or widen the monitor to 2 blocks. (composition) reframe to a 3/4-front angle from beside the monitor so Juniper's face and the screen are both visible, and keep Marlow's monitor out of frame. (lighting) add a teal light from the monitor on the agent's face and desk, and a warm desk lamp. (character) show the face, let the head bob or look between keyboard and screen, and give the skins a cleaner hair silhouette.

Strengths: a warm lounge-plus-studio with beams, chained lanterns, clerestory windows, labelled bookshelves, desk status lamps (brass/teal/clay) and Marlow's big log screen. The space feels lived in. Problems: the brief asks for 3+ agents working at stations, but only Wren is clearly visible, and she is lounging on a sofa. Rowan is just a nameplate floating over a bookshelf with no body. Juniper is a sliver behind her monitor. Tove can't be seen. The nameplates collide: Tove's overlaps the '!' and Wren's, and a status lamp cuts into Tove's text. Chunky dark stair-sofas fill the bottom 40% of a wide-angle frame and draw the eye away from the work. Also about 10 identical chain lanterns. FIXES: (composition/clarity) move the camera to a standing-height corner aimed at the desk row, with FOV around 70, so 3-4 agents are seen full-body at distinct stations (desk, library lectern, task wall). Push the sofas to the frame edge or drop them out of frame. (legibility) add nameplate collision avoidance (vertical stacking with leader lines) and distance-based scaling. (character) move Rowan to an aisle lectern where his body is visible. If Wren is waiting on the user, she should stand near the podium facing the camera with a pulsing '!'. (cohesion) cut the lantern count in half and mix in hidden ceiling lights between the beams.

Strengths: Marlow is the most appealing character, with glasses, a beard and a navy suit with a brass pin. The clay '!' above him, the lectern with paper, the bell and ember particles tell a small story. Problems: the decision isn't actually open. The question is truncated twice ('about `not...', 'completed notes ...') and no answer choices are shown, so the user can't act from this view. The nameplate is dark and the bubble is cream, two UI languages side by side. The thin glowing salmon outline around the alcove reads as a debug selection box rather than a crafted element. The bottom 30% of the frame is empty birch floor, and the alcove's right half is empty dark wood. The secondary Kit screen on the right is tiny and angled. Marlow stands rigidly with his arms down. The light is flat, and the podium doesn't pop from the dark alcove. FIXES: (clarity/legibility) show the full question wrapped over 3 lines, plus option keycaps (e.g. [Y] count them / [N] skip / [R] reply). Use one nameplate and bubble style (cream paper, brass border). (composition) push in and lower the camera so Marlow and the podium fill the lower two-thirds. Fill the alcove's right half with a clay-shaded decision lamp or plant. (lighting/cohesion) replace the glowing outline with in-world light: a pulsing clay lamp above the podium, candles, a hidden strip under the shelf. (aliveness) Marlow turns his head toward the user and raises a hand while waiting.

Strengths: a cream paper console with large crisp text, colour-coded agent names with avatar heads, per-agent left bars, needs-you lines highlighted in red, a '6 on shift' header with avatar status dots, and working @-mention autocomplete with ghost text. The state is readable fast. Problems: the autocomplete popup is dark grey, close to the default Minecraft look, and clashes with the cream panel. It also sits on top of the bottom-left of the log. The input bar spans the full width while the log panel is about 63%, so the two misalign. The right third of the frame is a blurry close-up azalea block. Marlow's world nameplate peeks out behind the top of the panel. Lines wrap mid-thought ('2 / files)', 'u / flag.') with no hanging indent. FIXES: (cohesion) restyle the autocomplete as a cream card with a brass border, anchored above the caret in the input. (composition) left-align the log panel and input to one width, or make the log full width. Darken or blur the world behind the console and hide world nameplates while it is open. Choose a camera position with a calm backdrop. (lighting) add a soft vignette or warm dim behind the UI. (character/aliveness) a small typing indicator next to the agent being addressed ('Juniper is typing...'), and new log lines sliding in.

Strengths: the strongest shot, close to ship quality. A paper panel with a brass frame, clay accents, a clear title and 'Waiting for you' state, branch chips, matching totals (+26 -5 = +19-4 plus +7-1), a file list, agent notes, a syntax-highlighted diff with line numbers and hunk header, and well-weighted actions (clay Merge, neutral Request changes, red Reject) with key hints. Problems: the cryptic 'd3' next to 'Waiting for you'. The redundant 'wren-t4' id. '»' wrap markers add noise. Empty space under the notes column. The only life is two tiny avatars. FIXES: (character) a larger Wren portrait with an expression, or a small live 3D head. Show the reviewer's mini-avatar beside 'Rowan reviewed'. (aliveness) a gentle pulse on the 'Waiting for you' dot, and a check mark animating next to 'tests pass'. Also replace 'd3' with 'decision 1 of 2' or drop it, and use the empty notes space for a test summary (17 pass).

Strengths: a polished Memory library. Tabs with counts, a note list with author, scope and age, a rich detail pane with Goal, Approach and Tasks, brass-tinted inline code chips, status-dot task list, a clear 'blocked: needs Blendi', and key hints. Problems: t4 has a brass ('thinking') dot here, a grey dot on the task wall and clay in the nameplate/diff. The same state shows in three colours. The trailing dots after '(after t2)' are cryptic. The last task row is cut mid-glyph at the bottom edge. The left list leaves its bottom 40% empty. Agents appear only as tiny avatars, and nothing moves. FIXES: (clarity) unify the status palette (t4 clay = waiting on user). Render dependencies as 'after t2 [done]' text chips instead of bare dots. Fade the bottom of the scroll area instead of clipping a line. (character) larger author avatars on the list rows. (aliveness) highlight recently updated notes with a fading clay underline and show a 'Kit is writing...' live indicator when an agent edits memory.

Strengths: the interior reads as lit through the windows. The atrium chandeliers, goal panel and desk monitors glow faintly, and the cupola windows have small lights, so it tells a 'studio working late' story. Problems: vanilla night light leaves the facade, roof and garden muddy and desaturated. The deepslate wing roof melts into the black sky and the silhouette is lost. The window light doesn't spill onto the porch or lawn. Only two path lanterns are visible, giving small light pools. There are no figures in the windows. Nothing outside shows status. The framing copies the day shot, dead lawn included. FIXES: (lighting) put light blocks just inside the windows and under the eaves so warm light spills out. Add soft lanterns along both paths and the porch steps. Add a lantern line or copper ridge light so the roof separates from the sky. (clarity/legibility) a cupola beacon colored by overall state (clay pulse = 2 need you), visible from across the meadow. (character/aliveness) agent silhouettes moving past lit windows, fireflies or particles over the garden, chimney smoke lit from below. (composition) a lower, closer angle, with the lit tower glazing on a third and the garden as a dark foreground frame.

overall: Not shippable against the bar. No shot has every axis at 8 or above. The two full-screen modals (qa08 diff review, qa09 memory library) are close to ship quality: cohesive paper/ink/clay/brass styling, crisp text, clear state. Their only shortfalls are character and aliveness. The in-world shots score 3-7. They are held back by flat vanilla lighting with no golden hour or hidden warm light, the lack of life and status signals on the exterior, framing that leaves dead space or slices key elements at the edges, nameplates that cover monitors and collide with each other, and ellipsis truncation on the most important text (goal, decision question, code lines). Two UI languages run side by side: dark charcoal for the goal panel, nameplates and autocomplete, cream paper everywhere else. Status colours are inconsistent: t4 is grey on the task wall, brass in the library and clay on the nameplate and diff. The best in-world details are the desk status lamps, Marlow's design, and the task-card information design. A typical r/Minecraft viewer would see a competent cozy build with good mod UI, not a showcase. The exterior architecture (lumpy tower roof, mismatched roofs, raw terrain) and the vanilla lighting are what keep it from looking like a real product.
